deck: The Venice most visitors never see. Tell me which of these sound like you and I’ll build the days around them.

doors.p: An early private visit of the Basilica and the Doge’s Palace with a guide, past the lines. A thousand years of Venetian power, in gold and stone, while the square is still quiet.

doors.h: Palaces that don’t open to the public
doors.p: Private keys to Venetian palaces, historic villas and churches that usually stay closed, with the art inside them all to yourself.
A private boat as the light goes gold over the city. It’s the view of Venice you came for, without a single other tourist in the frame.
The three islands of the lagoon by private water taxi, with a guide. A glassblowing demonstration in a working furnace on Murano, the colored houses of Burano, and a long lunch I reserve for you.

The Rialto market in the morning, then the bacari, the little wine bars where locals stand at the counter for cicchetti and a glass of something regional. With a private guide who knows which ones are worth it.
A private class with an expert artisan in a real workshop, decorating a mask the traditional way. You leave with one of your own, and a very good story.
A private car from the lagoon straight up into the mountains, so the two halves of the trip feel like one.
